transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-04
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Recording ID: ff-20250904-veridian-ssoprovision-01
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Veridian InfoSec), Dev Patel (Veridian Platform), Aisha Khan (Veridian SRE)

Summary (auto): quick walkthrough of SAML/SCIM provisioning flows, confirmation of required SAML attributes and ACS endpoints, SCIM provisioning deltas (PATCH vs PUT), discussion on least-privilege RBAC roles and service account patterns, KMS/customer-managed key options, and audit log retention/forwarding. Agreed to exchange IdP metadata and schedule pilot.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. I'm Jordan, AE on the account. With me is Priya, our SE.
[00:27] Priya Raman: Hi all. Quick agenda: SAML assertion mapping, SCIM provisioning semantics, RBAC role matrix, and then a short run through of KMS and audit/logging integrations. We'll pause for questions along the way.
[01:03] Marta Ruiz: Great. For context, Veridian's timeline is we want SSO in place for initial 50 users for the pilot in Q4, and then expand. Primary concerns: least privilege, auditability, and where keys live — we have constraints on data residency.
[01:25] Dev Patel: Also network-wise, if we go private we need to know peering and ingress ports; but first we want IdP integration to be smooth.
[01:40] Priya Raman: Understood. Quick question — are you using Okta as your IdP for the pilot?
[01:46] Marta Ruiz: Yes Okta to start, but we might use AWS IAM Identity Center down the road.
[01:52] Jordan Lee: Okta is pretty common; our SAML support covers typical ADFS/Okta/Ping setups. We'll need your IdP metadata XML, and the certificate that signs assertions.
[02:10] Aisha Khan: Will you accept an EntityID that's a custom URL? Our policy requires unique SP entity ids per environment.
[02:18] Priya Raman: Yes, SP entityID can be customized per environment. We'll also provide ACS URLs for both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows.
[02:35] Jordan Lee: One thing we often see is mismatch on NameID format. Do you prefer emailNameID or persistent?
[02:43] Marta Ruiz: Email is preferred for our user sync, but we can map persistent if required.
[03:00] Priya Raman: OK — on attributes we'll typically request: email, given_name, family_name, groups (if IdP sends groups). For groups we support both group sent as CSV or multi-valued attribute depending on IdP.
[03:20] Dev Patel: About groups, can Redwood's SCIM handle group membership changes quickly? We have teams that move users around frequently.
[03:29] Priya Raman: Yes, SCIM provisioning handles group add/remove. We implement PATCH semantics for delta updates so it doesn't re-provision whole users every time — that reduces churn and rate limits.
[03:45] Marta Ruiz: Speaking of rate limits — what are your SCIM rate limits? We have automated onboarding scripts we run in bursts.
[03:52] Priya Raman: Default is modest, but for Dedicated/Private deployments we can accommodate higher throughput. For hosted customers we negotiate burst windows; for the pilot we'll profile your onboarding and recommend throttling config.
[04:10] Jordan Lee: Another common ask: SCIM bearer token rotation. We'll support rotating the token without downtime by allowing a short overlap window during rotation.
[04:26] Aisha Khan: Good. On RBAC — we want least-privilege. Can you walk through your typical roles and what they map to API permissions?
[04:36] Priya Raman: Sure. Typical roles we ship with: Owner (full admin), Admin (manage config & users), Operator (deploy/run inference, view metrics), Observer (read-only dashboards), and Service Account (API-only, scoped). We recommend mapping teams to Operator and using service accounts for automation.
[05:00] Dev Patel: We need the ability to create scoped service accounts that can only call embedding endpoints, not model management or billing APIs. Is that supported?
[05:08] Priya Raman: Yes — our token scopes include: generate, embeddings, manage-models, billing-read, billing-write, admin. You can compose a token with only 'embeddings' and 'generate' for ingestion pipelines.
[05:25] Jordan Lee: And everything is audited — actions tied to token or SSO user in the audit log. Speaking of logs, what's your retention and can we forward to our SIEM?
[05:36] Marta Ruiz: Retention should be 12 months for audit logs; we want to send them to Splunk.
[05:43] Priya Raman: We retain detailed audit logs for 90 days by default on hosted, longer on enterprise plans. For Dedicated/Private you can choose retention and we support syslog/forwarding to Splunk/Datadog or pulling via API. We'll include examples in the compliance pack.
[06:05] Aisha Khan: Are logs PII redacted by default? We don't want user emails in certain log tiers.
[06:12] Priya Raman: We can redact or hash attributes at ingestion; also you can configure which fields are stored in long-term retention. We'll cover that in the compliance docs.
[06:29] Dev Patel: Encryption — we want customer-managed keys (CMK) for model artifacts and token secrets. What options?
[06:36] Priya Raman: For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer optional CMEK (customer-managed encryption keys) via cloud KMS integrations — AWS KMS, Google KMS. For hosted, we manage keys but can setup envelope encryption with your KMS under contract.
[06:58] Jordan Lee: Important to note: if you require on-prem HSM, that's part of a Private engagement and we can scope that.
[07:08] Marta Ruiz: Good. Data residency — we need data for EU users to remain in eu-west-1. How do you handle residency?
[07:15] Priya Raman: We have region pinning for both hosted and dedicated; for Private it's entirely in your VPC. We can guarantee processing in a specified region and provide attestations.
[07:30] Jordan Lee: Switching back to SAML details — Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URLs: we'll provide one per environment. Also, what's your recommended session timeout for SSO sessions?
[07:40] Priya Raman: Default session TTL is one hour, but you can configure up to 24 hours or integrate with IdP SSO session management for SAML single logout.
[07:54] Marta Ruiz: We prefer 2-hour timeout. Also we need SAML single logout so that when we disable a user centrally sessions terminate across services.
[08:03] Priya Raman: We support SLO but it's IdP-dependent — we recommend testing IdP-initiated SLO in your staging tenant.
[08:14] Dev Patel: On the SCIM schema: do you support custom attributes? We have an internalEmployeeID and cost_center we'd like to map.
[08:23] Priya Raman: Yes, we accept extension attributes — we can map custom attributes under scim 'urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User' or a custom schema. We'll share an example payload.
[08:40] Aisha Khan: Back to RBAC — can we have role hierarchies and least-privilege overrides per team? For example, Team A needs model deploy but not billing.
[08:50] Priya Raman: You can create custom roles in the console with fine-grained permissions. We also support project-scoped roles so you can limit deploy rights to a project or model namespace.
[09:06] Jordan Lee: Operational note — if you want to automate role provisioning from your identity provider we support SCIM group-to-role mapping. So if an Okta group 'redwood-operators' maps to the Operator role, on SCIM sync the user gets that role.
[09:21] Marta Ruiz: That sounds ideal. We will have group-based role assignment. What about service account rotation and ephemeral tokens?
[09:30] Priya Raman: We offer short-lived tokens for service accounts (configurable TTL) and recommend rotating longer-lived service tokens monthly. There's an API to rotate programmatically.
[09:44] Dev Patel: Anything about API key leakage protections? We want ability to restrict keys by IP range.
[09:51] Priya Raman: For Dedicated/Private we support IP allowlists and network policies. For hosted, we do IP allowlisting per-organization and token scoping.
[10:05] Jordan Lee: Let's talk about a few edge cases we see in enterprise: duplicate emails across different identity providers, name collisions, and SCIM provisioning conflict resolution.
[10:16] Priya Raman: Our merge logic prefers stable unique id from IdP if available (persistent NameID or user.externalId in SCIM). Otherwise email is fallback. We also have a manual conflict resolution UI for admins.
[10:32] Aisha Khan: Good to know. For the pilot we will use email as canonical but we'll send persistent IDs later.
[10:40] Marta Ruiz: Quick aside on compliance — do you have a SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certification? Can you redact PII before we review?
[10:51] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certs. We'll send the compliance pack; we'll redact sensitive customer PII in the document we send for review.
[11:05] Priya Raman: We'll also include sample audit logs and the schema so you can see what fields are captured.
[11:14] Dev Patel: One more on logging — can you include request IDs and trace IDs in logs to correlate across services?
[11:21] Priya Raman: Absolutely, every user action includes request_id, trace_id, and associated user or service account.
[11:33] Jordan Lee: Now a quick walk through of the onboarding checklist I prepared — step 1: exchange IdP metadata & test tenant. Step 2: map groups -> roles in SCIM. Step 3: validate SCIM provisioning with sample users. Step 4: set up CMK/KMS if required. Step 5: enable audit forwarding to Splunk and validate retention. Step 6: pilot rollout.
[11:58] Marta Ruiz: That aligns with our internal checklist. For step 4 we need specifics on KMS integration and any key rotation impacts on stored artifacts.
[12:08] Priya Raman: For CMEK, key rotation is compatible — we use envelope encryption, so rotating the data key is a two-step process and we document downtime/impact. For model artifacts we can re-encrypt in background for most objects; we'll include expected timings.
[12:30] Dev Patel: On the pilot size — 50 users, two service accounts, one model namespace. We'll want to run a stress test for SCIM + onboarding and a small token load test for inference. Can Redwood run a short benchmark?
[12:45] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can run a scoped benchmark in your staging env or we can run sim in our dedicated environment. We'll coordinate offline to decide.
[13:00] Marta Ruiz: What about SAML signature algorithms? We mandate SHA-256 for assertions.
[13:07] Priya Raman: We support SHA-1 and SHA-256 but will enforce SHA-256 for enterprise.
[13:15] Aisha Khan: Are there any limitations around length of group attribute or number of group memberships? We have a user who belongs to 800 groups — will that be a problem?
[13:25] Priya Raman: Very large group cardinality can cause payload size issues; best practice is mapping to a subset or use group sync by membership attribute. We'll help you design a mapping that limits size and uses group-of-groups if needed.
[13:44] Dev Patel: For SCIM PATCH semantics, do you support operations: add, remove, replace?
[13:50] Priya Raman: Yes we support RFC7644 PATCH operations with add/remove/replace, and bulk endpoints for initial seeding.
[14:02] Jordan Lee: Quick note about metadata cert rotation — if you rotate signing certs on IdP side, you'll need to update metadata on our side. We can accept metadata XML or manual cert upload.
[14:16] Marta Ruiz: We'll share metadata XML.
[14:20] Priya Raman: On the RBAC matrix template — Jordan will share a starting template. We'd like team feedback so we can propose default mappings.
[14:31] Jordan Lee: I'll send the template and the compliance pack after the call.
[14:36] Aisha Khan: Any single-sign-on audit hooks? We need to show last login per user in our portal.
[14:43] Priya Raman: Yes, last_login is an attribute we store and include in the user API and audit logs.
[14:52] Dev Patel: Network question again — for private deployment, what ports and egress are required?
[14:59] Priya Raman: We'll share a minimal network diagram: typically HTTPS outbound to our registry endpoints, and internal ports for health checks; for peering we request a route table entry and security group allowing specific ports. We'll attach a template.
[15:14] Jordan Lee: Any regulatory constraints on data residency beyond region pinning?
[15:20] Marta Ruiz: Not beyond storing EU PII in EU. We do need proof of data at rest encryption and key management processes.
[15:28] Priya Raman: We'll include KMS attestation and encryption-in-transit docs.
[15:35] Dev Patel: Ok last quick tech nuance — do you store KV cache contents on disk in clear or encrypted form? We worry about model context exposure.
[15:45] Priya Raman: KV cache is encrypted at rest; on Private deployments you can bring your own encryption keys. For hosted, KV cache is encrypted using server-side keys and we can enable envelope with customer keys on enterprise plans.
[16:00] Jordan Lee: Time check — we're about halfway. Any critical items we haven't covered?
[16:05] Marta Ruiz: One more: we require periodic access reviews and an API to list active sessions and tokens so we can audit and revoke.
[16:12] Priya Raman: We provide an API to list sessions, active tokens, and to revoke tokens. Also scheduled access review exports can be generated.
[16:26] Aisha Khan: Great. Can you support SCIM deltas for deprovisioning within 5 minutes SLA? We need quick revocation for compromised users.
[16:36] Priya Raman: For Dedicated/Private we can meet a 5-minute target. For hosted customers we'd aim for near real-time but will measure during pilot.
[16:48] Dev Patel: Regarding logging fields — can you include the actor type (human/service) and role at time of action?
[16:56] Priya Raman: Yes, logs will include actor_type and actor_role fields.
[17:10] Jordan Lee: We're circling back to next steps and responsibilities. I'll read out the action items.
[17:18] Jordan Lee: Action 1: Marta to share IdP metadata by Sept 8. Action 2: Priya to draft SCIM attribute map by Sept 10. Action 3: Jordan to send compliance pack by Sept 5. Action 4: Dev to share network/VPC constraints by Sept 9.
[17:40] Marta Ruiz: Sounds good. A couple tiny risks: our procurement team needs pricing for Dedicated if pilot goes long. Also we may need an addendum for KMS usage.
[17:52] Jordan Lee: We'll include pricing tiers and a KMS addendum in the follow-up.
[18:00] Aisha Khan: Can we get a short demo of the SCIM mapping UI before we finalize?
[18:06] Priya Raman: Yes — we'll schedule a 30-min demo next week showing the console mapping & test provisioning.
[18:14] Dev Patel: For the pilot we also want a test plan (users, operations, load). Can Redwood supply a template?
[18:20] Jordan Lee: We'll send a test plan template along with the onboarding checklist.
[18:28] Marta Ruiz: Quick note on compliance docs — please remove internal Redwood customer names from the SOC 2 doc before we distribute internally.
[18:36] Jordan Lee: We'll produce a redacted copy for you.
[18:42] Priya Raman: Anything else from Veridian?
[18:46] Marta Ruiz: No, that's it for now.
[18:50] Aisha Khan: Thanks everyone.
[18:53] Jordan Lee: Thanks — we'll follow up via email with artifacts.
[18:58] Priya Raman: Bye.

Recap / explicit next steps at end of call:
- Jordan to send SOC2/ISO compliance pack (redacted) and RBAC template by 2025-09-05.
- Marta to provide IdP metadata + test tenant credentials by 2025-09-08.
- Priya to draft SCIM mapping and example payloads by 2025-09-10 and schedule console mapping demo.
- Dev to share VPC/network constraints and pilot test plan inputs by 2025-09-09.

End of transcript.
